sections.sectionSummaryBrief: This section contains the opening heading and date for the maamar "Atah Hareisa Lada'as" from Simchas Torah 5737.

translations.translation: With the help of Heaven.
The day of Simchas Torah, 5737 (1976).

sections.sectionSummaryBrief: This section introduces the verse "Atah Hareisa Lada'as" as the first of seventeen verses recited before the hakafos, explaining it is the head that includes them all, and questions its connection to the joy of Shemini Atzeres and Simchas Torah.

translations.translation: "You have been shown to know that Hashem, He is the Elokim; there is none else besides Him."
Now, this verse is the first of the seventeen verses
that are recited before the hakafos (circumambulations).
And it can be said,
that this verse is also the head of all the seventeen verses, encompassing them,
similar to the head which encompasses all the limbs of the body.
And it is necessary to understand the connection of "Atah Hareisa" etc. to the hakafos.
And even more so, explanation is needed according to what was said by my revered father-in-law, the Rebbe,
that the matter of reciting the verses before the hakafos is to bring reasons
for the joy of Shemini Atzeres and Simchas Torah
[similar to the verses of Malchiyos, Zichronos, and Shofaros],
for seemingly,
what is the connection of "Atah Hareisa Lada'as" etc. to the joy of Shemini Atzeres and Simchas Torah?
And especially since "Atah Hareisa Lada'as" occurred at the time of the Giving of the Torah,
which is on the festival of Shavuos.

sections.sectionSummaryBrief: This section explains that the need to bring proof from Torah for the hakafos indicates their supreme loftiness, contrasting the limited joy of the Simchas Beis HaSho'eivah with the unlimited joy of Simchas Torah in which all Israel are equal.

translations.translation: And this will be understood by prefacing what is explained elsewhere
regarding the matter of reciting the verses of Malchiyos, Zichronos, and Shofaros,
that the need to bring proof from the Torah for these matters,
is,
because they are matters of the utmost loftiness.
And from this it is also understood regarding the recitation of the verses before the hakafos,
that the need to bring proof from the Torah for the matter of the hakafos is because it is a matter of the utmost loftiness.
And as explained in Likkutei Torah,
that the fact that in the Torah only the wine libation is written, but not the water libation, which is only a halachah l'Moshe mi'Sinai,
is,
because the water libation is a matter of the utmost loftiness that cannot be clothed in the letters of the Written Torah,
and the fact that the matter of the hakafos is not even explicated in the Oral Torah and is only a custom is because the matter of the hakafos is even loftier than the water libation.
And this is also
that the joy of the Simchas Beis HaSho'eivah,
despite being a very great joy,
to the extent that one who has not seen the Simchas Beis HaSho'eivah has never seen joy in his life,
nevertheless,
it is within measure and limitation.
As is also understood from the fact that in the joy of the Simchas Beis HaSho'eivah,
only pious men and men of deed would dance,
and all the people would come to see and hear,
for this limitation regarding those who rejoice in this joy is because the entirety of this joy
(even among the pious men and men of deed)
is within measure and limitation.
However, on Simchas Torah,
and especially during the hakafos,
the custom of Israel
(which is Torah)
is that all of Israel
(men, women, and children)
rejoice in it,
because this joy is above measure and limitation.
[And to add,
that the hakafos the second time
(on the night of Simchas Torah)
their custom is to be with greater joy than the first time
(on the night of Shemini Atzeres),
for when the joy is in the same measure as in the previous hakafos,
without addition and increase,
it is not complete joy,
because it has become stale.
And the Alter Rebbe writes in his Siddur,
that even when he had already conducted the hakafos with joy in his synagogue,
when he came to a synagogue where they had not yet finished the hakafos, he would sing and rejoice with them as well].
And it can be said that its parallel is the service of "Make Me king over you" on Rosh HaShanah,
in which all of Israel are equal,
as it is stated,
"You are standing today, all of you," etc.,
for on the day of Rosh HaShanah, all ten categories of Israel
(from your heads, your tribes, to your woodcutters and water drawers)
are as one unit, like one.
